events.title: B programming language created at Bell Labs
events.summary: Ken Thompson developed B circa 1969 as a typeless systems language derived from BCPL for early Unix on the PDP-7.
events.about: B was the stepping stone between BCPL and C — word-oriented, minimal, meant for Unix kernel and tool development on memory-constrained PDP machines. Thompson wrote the first B compiler after Fortran proved too heavy for the PDP-7. Dennis Ritchie then evolved B into C by adding types.

narrative.whyChosen: Unix needed a systems language lighter than Fortran; B was the experiment that proved the approach before C added types.
narrative.whyImportant: B established the BCPL→B→C lineage that defines systems programming to this day.
narrative.problemSolved: PDP-7 had tiny memory; Multics-era languages were too large to compile or run on the new Unix hardware.

sources.title: Ritchie — The Development of the C Language (B created 1969–70)
